prompt: Explain the fundamental physical difference between 'mass' and 'amount of substance'.
answer: Mass measures the quantity of matter in a body and its resistance to acceleration (inertia) in kilograms, whereas amount of substance is proportional to the number of elementary entities (particles) in the sample in moles.

mark_scheme.criterion: Mass measures inertia / resistance to acceleration / gravitational property (with SI unit kg).
Amount of substance measures / is proportional to the number of elementary entities / particles (with SI unit mol).

hints: Consider what property of an object determines its acceleration when a force acts on it.
Consider what property of an object simply counts how many particles are present.
solution: Mass is an SI base quantity that measures an object's inertia (its resistance to acceleration) and gravitational interaction, measured in kilograms. Amount of substance is an SI base quantity that measures the number of elementary entities (such as atoms, molecules, or ions) present in a sample, measured in moles. Two samples with equal mass can have completely different amounts of substance if their particle masses differ.
teacher_walkthrough: Clarify that mass depends on particle mass, while amount of substance depends purely on particle count.
Use the lead vs helium comparison (1 kg of helium has many more moles than 1 kg of lead).
